Sinus arrhythmia: In simple terms, although the heartbeat starts normally, the heart beats slowly and obviously. The origin of sinus rhythm has not changed, but the rhythm is not uniform. The PP interval difference in the same lead is >0.12s. . Sinus arrhythmia and sinus bradycardia exist simultaneously. A more common type of arrhythmia is related to the respiratory cycle, which is called respiratory sinus arrhythmia, which is more common in adolescents and generally has no clinical significance. Other rare sinus arrhythmia have nothing to do with breathing, such as non-ventricular contraction and blood discharge (ventricular phase) sinus arrhythmia and sinus node arrhythmia

Sinus tachycardia: tachycardia caused by increased cardiac self-discipline, also known as autonomic tachycardia. The frequency of tachycardia in adults is 101-190 beats/min, typically 101-150 beats/min. The frequency of sinus tachycardia in children can reach 200 beats per minute.

Sinus bradycardia: Sinus rhythm is slower than 60 times per minute called sinus bradycardia. Sinus node dysfunction, increased intracranial pressure, hypothyroidism, taking certain drugs (such as beta-blockers) cause sinus bradycardia, common in young people, athletes and sleep states

Ventricular pacing refers to the pacing of the ventricular contraction in the atrioventricular junction. At this time, the atrium has contracted, the mechanical contraction of both ventricles is stopped, and the ventricular resting time is usually 2.7 s or more.

When the sinus node or atrial dysfunction cannot be transmitted on time for some reason, the pacing point at the transition zone of the next level should be released from the atrioventricular junction to control the ventricle. If the atrioventricular junction area is also affected by the same cause as the sinoatrial node, and the escape is not possible, the ventricular pacemaker will activate the ventricle to form a ventricular escape. Continuous 3 or more ventricular escape, which constitutes ventricular escape rhythm, or ventricular autonomic rhythm, ventricular arrhythmia, ventricular self-heart rhythm and so on.

Before the sinus node impulse has not yet reached the ventricle, the ectopic rhythm of any part of the ventricle or the interventricular septum is prematurely emitted to cause depolarization of the ventricle, called ventricular premature contraction, referred to as early room.
